definition: Tazti is a speech recognition software package developed and sold by Voice Tech Group, Inc.
details: for Windows personal computers. The most recent package is version 3.2, which supports Windows 10, Windows 8.1, Windows 8 and Windows 7 64-bit editions. Earlier versions of Tazti supported Windows Vista and Windows XP. Tazti's primary features are playing PC video games by voice, controlling PC applications and programs by voice, and creating speech commands to trigger a browser to open web pages, or trigger the Windows operating system to open files, folders or programs. Earlier versions of Tazti included a lite Dictation feature that is eliminated from the latest version.

explainer.lead: Tazti is a speech recognition software package by Voice Tech Group, Inc. for Windows PCs, used to control games, applications, and system actions by voice. It matters for hands-free computer control, especially in gaming.

tiers.eli5: Software that lets you talk to your Windows computer to play games or open programs instead of using a mouse or keyboard.
tiers.practitioner: Users create speech commands to trigger browser pages or open files, folders, and programs. A pitfall is that version 3.2 supports only specific Windows versions (10, 8.1, 8, and 7 64-bit), with earlier versions for Vista and XP.
tiers.paperLevel: Tazti is a commercial speech recognition package; its primary features are voice control of PC video games, voice control of PC applications and programs, and creating speech commands to trigger browser or Windows actions. The most recent version is 3.2.

explainer.example: A player can say a command to open a web page or launch a game without using the keyboard.
